output.summary:
I stopped after the measurement step and am not submitting a change. No sink sub-step costs more than 8% on its own, and the step-2 fix the plan named, growing the local sink capacity, makes things about 30% slower.

The ablation code is temporary and must not be committed. It reads a flag from a session variable (`SET VARIABLE dbe_ablate=N`) in `src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp` and `src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp`; the harness will reset the tree.

Test query: `SELECT max(s) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey k, sum(l_quantity) s FROM lineitem GROUP BY k)`, 15M groups, 8 threads, hot runs via `dbe-tool sql`. Timings are wall time; the machine is noisy (about ±5%, first run of each batch dropped).

| Variant | Wall time | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | ~455 ms | – |
| (a) skip sink InitializeStates | ~710 ms | slower (states left as garbage; tells us nothing) |
| (b) skip sink UpdateAggregates | ~430 ms | -6% |
| (c) local sink capacity 1<<22 (no abandon/repartition) | ~570–630 ms | about +30% |
| (d) no HLL / no adaptation | ~430 ms | at noise level |
| (e1) skip finalize Combine entirely | ~345 ms | -24% |
| (e2) source Scan emits nothing | ~460 ms | 0 |
| skip_lookups forced from the start | ~820–1100 ms | much worse |

Splitting the finalize Combine further:

| Finalize variant | Wall time | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Scan only (no probe, no append) | ~340 ms | – |
| No CombineStates | ~458 ms | CombineStates costs about 0 |
| No append or InitializeStates (dummy row pointers) | ~385 ms | new-row materialisation costs about 70 ms (15%) |

That leaves the finalize probe at about 45 ms (10%).

Radix bits:

| Radix bits | Wall time | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Force 8, ignoring the row-width cap | ~440 ms | -3%, at noise level |
| 9 or 10 | ~600 ms | about +30% |

The only part over 8% is the finalize re-materialisation (about 15%). The fix for that is an in-place finalize, which E0002 already tried with no gain on q18. Even a perfect fix there is worth at most about 6% on q18, since the aggregate is only part of the query. I did not repeat it.
output.generality: No change shipped. The measurements apply to any high-cardinality parallel hash aggregate where the input is clustered on the key, so each thread-local table already deduplicates almost completely: the sink costs are spread across many steps, and finalize re-materialisation is the largest single one (about 15%).
output.notes:
Dead ends, all measured:
- Growing local_sink_capacity (fewer abandons): +30%. A bigger thread-local table hurts cache more than the abandons cost, so the DecideAdaptation capacity rule should not be built.
- More radix bits (9 or 10): +30%. Forcing 8 bits by ignoring the row-width cap: -3%, noise.
- Forcing skip_lookups: much worse.
- HLL, source Scan and finalize CombineStates: each about 0.
- Skipping sink UpdateAggregates saves only 6%, so an InitializeStates/UpdateStates fast path has a ceiling of about 6% on the isolated aggregate, and less on q18.

Where the finalize Combine time goes: about 115 ms of the ~455 ms total. Of that, new-row append plus InitializeStates is about 70 ms and the probe into the partition table (~2 MB) is about 45 ms. The in-place finalize (E0002) is the only fix aimed at the append part; it already failed on q18.

Remaining sink time is about 225 ms (the ~340 ms scan-only-finalize run minus ~115 ms for the plain scan). It is spread across hashing, probing the local table, the partitioned append and the aggregate update, with no single dominant part.

Tooling tip: dbe-tool sql accepts several statements in one call, so `SET VARIABLE dbe_ablate=N; <query>; <query>...` works. Reading the flag through ClientConfig::GetUserVariable lets one build test many variants. Writing to /tmp is blocked.

Suggestion: the aggregate looks close to what this design can do for this shape. Later rounds may get more from other q18 operators: the 0.44 s and 0.24 s hash joins, and the orders scan at 0.32 s CPU.
